:::{#exm-exp-reg}
#### Exponential regression with one binary covariate

Let $x_1 = 1$ for patients on a standard treatment
and $x_1 = 0$ for patients on a new treatment,
and suppose $\beta_0 = \logf{0.025}$ and $\beta_1 = \logf{4}$,
with time measured in weeks.
By @eq-exp-reg-haz:

$$
\ba
\haz(t \mid x_1 = 0)
&= \expf{\beta_0}
&& \text{(exponential regression hazard with } x_1 = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0.025
&& \text{(} \expf{\logf{0.025}} = 0.025 \text{)} \\
\haz(t \mid x_1 = 1)
&= \expf{\beta_0 + \beta_1}
&& \text{(exponential regression hazard with } x_1 = 1 \text{)} \\
&= \expf{\beta_0} \cdot \expf{\beta_1}
&& \text{(product rule for exponentials)} \\
&= 0.025 \cdot 4
&& \text{(evaluate each factor)} \\
&= 0.1
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

Each group's mean event time is the reciprocal of its hazard rate,
as derived in @sec-psm-exp-dist:
$1/0.025 = 40$ weeks on the new treatment
and $1/0.1 = 10$ weeks on the standard treatment.

:::
